questions.prompt: According to CDC and WHO guidance, adults should aim for at least how many minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week?
choices: 30''60 minutes
75''150 minutes
150''300 minutes
400''600 minutes
questions.explain: CDC and WHO both cite 150''300 minutes/week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity for adults.

questions.prompt: CDC and WHO guidance recommends muscle-strengthening activities on how many days per week for adults?
choices: 1 day
2 or more days
4 days
Every day only
questions.explain: Both CDC and WHO recommend muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days per week.

questions.prompt: Which statement best matches public health guidance on sedentary behavior?
choices: Sitting for long periods has no health impact if you exercise once a week
Breaking up long sitting periods with light movement can reduce health risks
Only vigorous exercise reduces sedentary risk
Sedentary time matters only for older adults
questions.explain: Public guidance emphasizes reducing prolonged sedentary time and breaking it up with movement.

questions.prompt: Which approach is most consistent with injury prevention guidance for increasing training load?
choices: Make the biggest increase possible to adapt faster
Progress gradually with manageable increases
Avoid strength training entirely to prevent injury
Only change one workout every 6 months
questions.explain: Gradual progression helps reduce injury risk compared to sudden spikes in load.

questions.prompt: Why is recovery emphasized in injury prevention principles?
choices: Recovery is only for beginners
Adequate recovery supports musculoskeletal health and reduces risk
Recovery replaces the need for technique
Recovery matters only for endurance athletes
questions.explain: Adequate recovery supports tissue adaptation and helps reduce injury risk.
